about.en:
FLEX Global is the U.S. Department of State's merit-based high-school exchange that merges the Future Leaders Exchange (FLEX, 30+ years) and the Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES, almost 25 years). It is implemented by American Councils for International Education with AFS, Amideast and iEARN. Türkiye is one of 31 countries in the 2027-28 cycle. Finalists live with a screened volunteer host family, attend a U.S. high school for the full year, do community service and take part in 'American Excellence' activities on business, technology and entrepreneurship.

Selection is free and runs in rounds: English testing, proctored essays, interviews with FLEX Global staff and a full application; final selection is made in the U.S., and English is only one factor. Finalists pass a medical check, learn their status in spring 2027, attend a pre-departure orientation at home in June or July, fly to the U.S. in August 2027 and return in May-June 2028. Placement anywhere in the U.S. is assigned, mostly in small towns and suburbs.

In Türkiye the programme is run by the national office (https://www.turkkulturvakfi.org.tr/flexglobal/, flexglobal.tur@afs.org). Türk Kültür Vakfı (AFS Türkiye) page is open for 2027-2028 applications but publishes no closing date; apply soon and confirm by phone (+90 212 246 4591).

Good academic standing, previous English study, U.S. J-1 visa eligibility and an international passport. Not eligible: students whose family has applied or plans to emigrate to the U.S.; usually not those who will have graduated before departure.

Finalists are told in spring 2027 and attend a pre-departure orientation in June-July

about.en:
FLEX Global is the U.S. Department of State's merit-based high-school exchange that merges the Future Leaders Exchange (FLEX, 30+ years) and the Kennedy-Lugar Youth Exchange and Study (YES). It is implemented by American Councils for International Education with AFS, Amideast and iEARN, and Mongolia is one of its 31 countries. Finalists spend a full year with a screened volunteer host family, attend a U.S. high school, do community service and take part in 'American Excellence' activities on business, technology and entrepreneurship.

The 2027-28 round for Mongolia closed on 2026-10-22 (eligible then: grades 9, 10 or 11, born 1 Jan 2010 - 15 Jul 2012). FLEX has recruited every autumn for decades, so the 2028-29 round is expected to open around August-September 2027 with an October deadline and a birth window roughly one year later; the national office (https://mongolia.americancouncils.org/) publishes the exact dates. Selection is free: English test, proctored essays, interview and a full application, with final selection in the U.S.

Use the year to prepare: keep grades high, practise English and short essays, and be ready to explain why you would be a good cultural ambassador. Finalists learn their status in spring and fly to the U.S. in August.

en: Full school year in the U.S. with a host family, fully funded
Merged FLEX + YES programme of the U.S. State Department, 31 countries
Free, merit-based selection: English test, essays, interview

eligibility.en: Citizens of Mongolia enrolled in secondary school in Mongolia: grades 9, 10 or 11, birth window for 2028-29 not yet published (2027-28 window was 1 Jan 2010 - 15 Jul 2012; expect it to move by about a year). Good academic standing, previous English study, U.S. J-1 visa eligibility and an international passport. Not eligible: students whose family has applied or plans to emigrate to the U.S.; usually not those who will have graduated before departure.

en: Follow the Mongolia FLEX Global office (https://mongolia.americancouncils.org/) and the FLEX Global Instagram for the 2028-29 announcement (around September 2027)
Check the new birth-date and grade window in the brochure when it is published
Register on ais.americancouncils.org/flexglobal and take the English test
Write the proctored essays and attend the interview if you advance
Submit the full application; finalists are announced in spring

costs.en: Free to apply. Covered: round-trip international and domestic travel, monthly allowance, host-family placement, U.S. school enrolment, orientations, local programme activities and medical insurance (excluding pre-existing conditions and dental). Not covered: passport costs, personal expenses beyond the stipend, excess baggage, internet/data plans.

about.en:

It is implemented by American Councils for International Education with AFS, Amideast and iEARN, and Moldova is one of its 31 countries. Finalists spend a full year with a screened volunteer host family, attend a U.S. high school, do community service and take part in 'American Excellence' activities on business, technology and entrepreneurship.

Check the new birth-date and grade window in the brochure when it is published
Register on ais.americancouncils.org/flexglobal and take the English test
Write the proctored essays and attend the interview if you advance
Submit the full application; finalists are announced in spring

Covered: round-trip international and domestic travel, monthly allowance, host-family placement, U.S. school enrolment, orientations, local programme activities and medical insurance (excluding pre-existing conditions and dental). Not covered: passport costs, personal expenses beyond the stipend, excess baggage, internet/data plans.

about.en:
AFS Japan's Year Programme sends Japanese high-school students to live with a host family and attend a local school for one school year in about 40 countries; AFS assigns the region, school and host family. The 74th term departs in 2027, and AFS is running an additional selection to fill remaining places.

Selection is an individual online interview from home on 5 November, 15 November or 3 December 2026; applicants to the U.S. also sit the ELTiS English test. Applications close at noon on 30 October, 4 November and 25 November respectively, but places are given first-come, first-served and each country closes when full. You need an Eiken (英検) certificate and a school recommendation; successful candidates must attend a residential orientation on 26-28 December 2026.

About 100 scholarship places from various sponsors are attached to the Year Programme, with scholarship results sent about two weeks after the exam.

en: Year at a local high school with a host family in ~40 countries
About 100 sponsored scholarship places
Online interview; last window closes 25 Nov 2026

eligibility.en: High-school students in Japan who meet the age window shown by the birth-date self-check in the online entry form. English proficiency certificate (Eiken) and school recommendation letter required.

en: Do the birth-date self-check on afs.or.jp to see which countries you can apply for
Submit the online entry by noon on the window's closing date (last: 25 Nov 2026)
Upload your Eiken certificate and school recommendation
Take the online interview (and ELTiS for the U.S.)
Attend the 26-28 Dec 2026 orientation if selected; apply for scholarships per the scholarship list

costs.en: Programme fee payable (see AFS Japan programme guide); about 100 scholarship places from sponsors reduce or cover costs.

score_reason: Well-run year exchange with scholarships, closing within a month.

summary.en: AFS Germany sends German school students on exchanges to 53 countries, and over 30% of participants receive a scholarship of 500 to 8,000 euros. Summer 2027 places are still open.

summary.ar: ترسل AFS ألمانيا طلاب المدارس الألمان في برامج تبادل إلى 53 دولة، ويحصل أكثر من 30% من المشاركين على منحة تتراوح بين 500 و8,000 يورو. ولا تزال مقاعد صيف 2027 متاحة.

about.en:
AFS Interkulturelle Begegnungen is one of Germany's largest non-profit school-exchange organisations. Students live with a volunteer host family and attend a local school in one of 53 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, North America and Oceania, for a few months up to a full school year.

More than 30% of AFS participants get a scholarship, usually partial (500-8,000 euros, at most 75% of the price). There are motivation scholarships, income-based scholarships (better chances below about 15,000 euros net household income per person), and named funds: Jürgen-Blankenburg, Helga-von-Hoffmann (Latin America), Asia Kakehashi+ (Japan), MercatorGO! (Türkiye), Czech Republic, volunteering, sports, Regenbogen (LGBTQIA+), non-Gymnasium schools and employer scholarships. Auslands-BAföG can also be used.

Apply for the programme first; after the contract confirmation you apply for a scholarship. If the scholarship is refused or too small you may withdraw free of charge within 14 days.

en: 53 destination countries
Over 30% of participants receive 500-8,000 euro scholarships
Free withdrawal if your scholarship is too low

eligibility.en: School students living in Germany, roughly 15-18 at departure (exact age by country). Scholarships: motivation-based or income-based; some reserved for specific countries, schools or groups.

en: Choose a country and programme on afs.de
Submit the AFS online application
After the contract confirmation, apply for a scholarship
Interview/selection weekend with AFS volunteers
Decide within 14 days of the scholarship decision

costs.en: Programme price per country (AFS price list); 10% due at contract signing. Scholarships 500-8,000 euros, max. 75% of costs; Auslands-BAföG possible.

score_reason: Large scholarship pool but only for Germany-based students; paid programme.

about.en:
AFS Österreich runs school exchanges to about 40 countries in Europe, Latin America, North America, Asia, Oceania and South Africa, from short programmes to a full school year, plus an apprentice exchange. Participants live with a host family and attend a local school.

Need-based AFS scholarships cover up to 70% of programme costs (not Global Choice); families must have gross annual income up to 90,000 euros and pay at least 30%. Selection uses a motivation letter and an interview in Vienna or online; being flexible on country improves your chances. Documents: motivation letter, asset declaration, parents' latest tax return and three months of payslips.

Deadlines: 31 March 2027 for the 2027-28 year programme and winter semester; 30 September for summer-semester departures. The 70th anniversary campaign '70 Jahre 70 Stipendien' adds extra places.

en: Up to 70% of costs covered for families up to 90,000 euros income
About 40 destination countries
Scholarship deadline 31 March 2027

eligibility.en: Students living in Austria aged about 14-18; scholarship requires gross family income up to 90,000 euros per year.

en: Choose a programme on afs.at
Use the afs.at application form and state that you want a scholarship
Send motivation letter, asset declaration, tax return and payslips by 31 March 2027
Attend the interview in Vienna or online

costs.en: Programme fee per country; scholarship up to 70% (participant pays at least 30%). Global Choice excluded.

score_reason: Generous need-based aid for Austrian residents; clear deadline.

about.en:
AFS Switzerland sends young people from Switzerland on school exchanges, programmes for apprentices, bridge-year programmes and short programmes to Europe, Latin America, North America, Asia, Africa and Oceania.

The classic AFS scholarship supports families with limited budgets (guideline: taxable income under CHF 80,000 and net assets under CHF 500,000) and covers 25-100% of the programme cost, decided by the Scholarship Committee after an interview. 'Destination Unknown' offers a reduced price regardless of income: you pick a semester or year and learn your country shortly before departure.

Submit the full AFS application with at least three destinations, the scholarship form, a motivation statement and tax documents. Deadline 15 November 2026 for summer 2027 departures (15 June 2027 for winter departures). Recipients report during the stay and volunteer for AFS afterwards.

'Destination Unknown' discount open to all

Interview with the Scholarship Committee

summary.ka: AFS Norway ნორვეგიელ მოზარდებს ექვს კონტინენტზე მასპინძელ ოჯახში 10-თვიან სასწავლო წელზე აგზავნის. რადგან AFS Lånekassen-ის მიერაა აღიარებული, მოსწავლეებს შეუძლიათ მიიღონ 50,000-70,000 ნორვეგიული კრონის სახელმწიფო გრანტი და AFS-ის საკუთარი სტიპენდიაც.

about.en:
AFS Norge offers a 10-month school year abroad with host-family placement in Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, North America and Oceania (autumn or winter departure), and 4-7-week language trips, for ages 14-18.

Because AFS is approved by Lånekassen (the Norwegian State Educational Loan Fund), exchange students can receive a grant of NOK 50,000-70,000 depending on destination (travel and living support, plus a means-tested basic grant), if the year is approved as VG2 with their school. AFS also has its own scholarship fund.

Applications are rolling via afs.no/soknad; the Lånekassen form opens in May of the year you travel.

Durations are 3-4, 4-6 or 8-11 months with spring or autumn departures, for ages 14-18+. Flights and insurance are included in the programme price. Applications for 2027 are open now and accepted year-round; places are filled in order, so popular destinations close early.

about.en:
The Voltaire Programme is a reciprocal one-to-one exchange run by the Franco-German Youth Office (DFJW/OFAJ). Pupils in grades 8, 9 or 10 who learn French (and French pupils learning German) spend six months living with their partner's family and attending school in France, then host the partner for six months at home. You can apply alone and be matched, or apply with a partner you already know.

It is one of the most immersive ways to become fluent in French or German without paying an agency: the families host each other and DFJW supports the exchange with preparation, support and a grant. Applications for the 2027/2028 campaign close on 6 November 2026; the next campaign opens on 1 August 2027.

eligibility.en: Pupils in grades 8, 9 or 10 in Germany learning French, and pupils in France learning German (the programme is for schools in the two countries).

costs.en: Families host each other; DFJW supports the exchange (grant details on programme-voltaire.org).

score_reason: Funded, deeply immersive; deadline next week.

about.en:
The Brigitte Sauzay Programme is a reciprocal exchange for pupils learning French (in Germany) or German (in France). Each partner spends at least three months with the other's family and attends school there, and the two stays can fall in one or two school years.

You find your partner yourself, for example through DFJW's online classifieds, agree dates with both schools and fill in the exchange dossier. DFJW pays a travel-cost grant if you apply online at least one month before the stay. It is a low-cost way to spend a term abroad without an agency.

about.en:
The Parlamentarisches Patenschafts-Programm (PPP) has been run since 1983 by the German Bundestag and the U.S. Congress (in the U.S. it is called CBYX). Each year it awards full scholarships to school students and young professionals from Germany to spend a year in the United States: school students live with a host family and attend a high school; young professionals study at a college and do an internship. Each scholar is sponsored by a Member of the Bundestag.

The 44th PPP (2027-28) closed on 11 September 2026. The 45th PPP (2028-29) is expected to open in May 2027; watch bundestag.de/ppp and apply online in that window. AFS Germany and other exchange organisations implement the programme.

about.en:
ASSIST is a non-profit that places international secondary students for a full academic year at member U.S. independent (mostly boarding) schools. The premier Sanderson Scholarship covers tuition, room and board for one year, valued up to US$84,000; the student pays about US$20,000 for the programme fee, flights, visa and mandatory U.S. health insurance, and donor-funded reductions of up to 80% are possible based on need. Fully funded places are rare and very competitive.

Applicants are 14-18, typically entering grade 10 or 11, with high English proficiency and university plans. Local offices exist in Austria, Bulgaria, Colombia, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Georgia, Germany, Hungary, Lithuania, Moldova, Norway, Poland, Serbia, Slovakia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and Türkiye; students elsewhere use the 'All Other Countries' route.

The application (form, transcripts, three teacher recommendations, parent statement, photos, short video) opens in July; full application due 1 December (Germany/Switzerland part by 15 November). Interviews run in December-January, decisions in January-February and school placements in March-April.

costs.en: Scholarship covers tuition, room and board (up to US$84,000). Family pays about US$20,000 (programme fee, travel, visa, insurance); up to 80% reduction possible on need.

summary.ar: ترسل AFS التشيك طلاب الثانوية التشيكيين إلى أكثر من 99 وجهة وتقدم منحًا جزئية: حتى 90% (250,000 كرونة) من صندوق Škoda Auto، ومنح صندوق المستقبل التشيكي الألماني، ومنح AAI لآسيا، وخصم 50% لبرنامج 'Destination Unknown'.

about.en:
AFS Czech Republic offers school exchanges of three months, a semester or a full year in more than 99 destinations, with host-family placement.

Scholarships include: Czech-German Future Fund (25,000-60,000 CZK for Germany), the Honorary Consulate in Stuttgart grant (75,000 CZK, Baden-Württemberg), the Škoda Auto Foundation (90% of the fee up to 250,000 CZK for students from Mladá Boleslav, Rychnov, Vrchlabí and Jilemnice areas), AAI scholarships for Türkiye, Hong Kong, Indonesia and China (40,800-98,400 CZK), 'Destination Unknown' (50% off semester programmes), host-family and volunteer discounts, plus the Jaroslava Moserová collection.

en: Up to 90% covered by the Škoda Auto fund
AAI scholarships for Asia
50% off with 'Destination Unknown'

eligibility.en: Secondary-school students living in the Czech Republic; each fund has its own criteria (region, destination, need).

en: Find a programme on afs.cz
Submit the AFS application form
Apply for the matching scholarship by its deadline
Attend selection

costs.en: Programme fee per destination; scholarships 25,000-250,000 CZK or 50-90% of the fee.

score_reason: Good partial funds; Czech residents only; deadlines vary.

about.en:
AFS Intercultura Brasil runs a Volunteer Work in Germany programme with partial scholarships: participants spend one year in Germany working in social projects while living in the local community. The 17th edition departs in the second semester of 2027 and has 6 places.

Previous editions covered food and accommodation, a minimum allowance of 100 euros per month and health insurance, for ages 18-27; confirm current conditions with AFS Brasil. Applications are open until 25 November 2026.

6 partial scholarships

summary.ar: برنامج لغوي صيفي مكثف وممول بالكامل من وزارة الخارجية الأمريكية لطلاب الجامعات الأمريكيين في العربية أو الصينية أو الهندية أو اليابانية أو الكورية أو الفارسية أو البرتغالية أو الروسية أو السواحيلية، في الخارج أو افتراضيًا. الموعد النهائي 17 نوفمبر 2026.

about.en:
The Critical Language Scholarship (CLS) Program is a U.S. government summer programme for American undergraduate and graduate students to study one of nine critical languages: Arabic, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Persian, Portuguese, Russian or Swahili. Institutes are held overseas (intensive classes, cultural activities, often homestays) or virtually for undergraduates.

It is a competitive, merit-based scholarship that covers programme costs for selected participants; some languages require prior study. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or nationals aged 18+ by 15 May 2027, enrolled in a U.S. degree programme and, for undergraduates, have completed one year of study by summer. Apply once per year for one language by 17 November 2026 (8 pm Eastern).

en: Nine critical languages, overseas or virtual
Fully funded by the U.S. State Department
Deadline 17 November 2026

eligibility.en: U.S. citizens/nationals, 18+ by 15 May 2027, enrolled in an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate degree programme (enrolled in fall 2026 and spring 2027 unless graduating in December); undergraduates must finish one full year of study before the programme; meet language prerequisites.

en: Check eligibility and language prerequisites on clscholarship.org
Choose one language
Submit the online application with essays and recommendations by 17 Nov 2026, 8 pm ET
Await selection results in spring 2027

costs.en: Fully funded for selected participants (programme costs paid by the U.S. Department of State).

score_reason: Fully funded language summer; U.S. students only; deadline soon.

about.en:
Tobitate! (Leap for Tomorrow) is a public-private study-abroad initiative of Japan's Ministry of Education (MEXT) run with JASSO and corporate donors. In the 'New Japan Representative Programme' 12th cohort for high-school students, 600 students (STEAM 140, sports/arts 120, 'my curiosity' 210, social issues 130) design their own stay abroad of 14 days to one year, starting between 10 July 2027 and 31 March 2028.

Support: monthly scholarship of 120,000 or 160,000 yen depending on destination (60,000 yen above the income threshold) and a preparation grant of 150,000 yen (Asia) or 250,000 yen (elsewhere). First-round applications run from early December 2026 to 21 January 2027; a second round (100 places) runs 1-21 April 2027.

en: 600 places for self-designed study abroad
120,000-160,000 yen per month + preparation grant
Apply Dec 2026 - 21 Jan 2027

eligibility.en: Japanese students (and equivalent) enrolled at high schools, secondary schools (upper), special-needs high schools, technical colleges (year 3 or below) or upper secondary specialised schools in Japan; incoming first-years can apply in round 2.

en: Read the 12th-cohort guidelines on the Tobitate site
Plan your study-abroad project and destination
Apply through the online system in the first round (by 21 Jan 2027) or second round (1-21 Apr 2027)
Pass the screening and attend pre-departure training

costs.en: Scholarship 120,000-160,000 yen/month plus 150,000-250,000 yen preparation grant.

score_reason: Large, generous programme; Japan-based students only.

about.en:
The university track of Tobitate!'s New Japan Representative Programme (19th cohort) funds 250 students (Innovator 50, STEAM 100, Diversity 100) to carry out a self-designed plan abroad - study, research, internship or fieldwork - lasting 28 days to one year (3+ months recommended), starting between 1 August 2027 and 31 March 2028.

Support matches the high-school track (120,000-160,000 yen per month, preparation grant 150,000-250,000 yen) plus up to 300,000 yen for tuition at the foreign institution. Applications are submitted via your university's office to JASSO between early December 2026 and 25 February 2027 (17:00); internal university deadlines are earlier.

Monthly stipend + up to 300,000 yen tuition
Apply via your university by 25 Feb 2027

Interview and selection; pre-departure training

about.en:
CEEPUS is an intergovernmental university exchange programme between Albania, Austria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia and Slovenia. Host countries pay a monthly grant (accommodation and living support) to incoming students and teachers.

Students who have fully completed two semesters at a CEEPUS university can go on network mobility (if their department belongs to a CEEPUS network) or as a 'freemover' (limited grants, in some countries only for the summer term). Citizenship of a member state is generally required. University networks apply for the 2027-28 year by 30 November 2026; students then apply online through ceepus.info for the mobility offered by their network or their National CEEPUS Office.

en: 16 member countries incl. Moldova, Serbia, Romania, Poland
Host-country grant covers living costs
Network or freemover routes

eligibility.en: Students enrolled at a university in a CEEPUS member country who have completed two semesters (one for intensive courses); generally citizens of a member state. Studying in your own country is not allowed.

en: Ask your international office whether your department is in a CEEPUS network
Register on ceepus.info
Apply online for network or freemover mobility by the deadline set for your term
Get the host university's acceptance letter

costs.en: Host-country monthly grant; travel normally not covered.

score_reason: Funded semester exchange for 16 countries; student deadlines vary.

Youth For Understanding Finland is a non-profit exchange organisation placing Finnish students with volunteer host families and local schools in North America (USA, Canada), Latin America (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Ecuador, Mexico, Paraguay, Uruguay), about 15 European countries, and Australia, South Africa, South Korea, Japan, China and Thailand.

Applications for the 2027-28 school year and the autumn 2027 semester are open from March 2026 until March 2027 (they close roughly six months before departure); spring 2028 semester applications run until September 2027. Applicants attend an interview. YFU Finland also awards a few partial scholarships each year (4,000 and 3,000 euros); the 2027-28 round closed in August 2026.

about.en:
YFU Eesti sends Estonian students aged 14-18 on exchange years with host families in countries such as Japan, Argentina, Brazil, France and Paraguay. Donor-funded scholarships help young people who could not otherwise afford the year.

About 15 one-time grants of 2,000-3,000 euros are awarded per year in two rounds (1 Oct - 15 Nov 2026 and 1 Feb - 14 Mar 2027), only for the year programme. You must have passed the YFU selection day, the contract interview and fundraising training; priority goes to families with limited means and large families outside Tallinn and Tartu. Send the application form and a motivation video to taotlused@yfu.ee; shortlisted students are interviewed.

en: About 15 grants of 2,000-3,000 euros
Priority for low-income and regional families
Deadline 15 November 2026

eligibility.en: Students in Estonia accepted to a YFU exchange-year programme (passed selection day and contract interview).

en: Pass YFU selection and the contract interview
Download the scholarship form from yfu.ee
Record a motivation video
Email both to taotlused@yfu.ee by 15 Nov 2026
Attend the interview if shortlisted

costs.en: Programme fee; grant of 2,000-3,000 euros deducted from it.

score_reason: Clear grants for Estonian residents; deadline 15 Nov.

about.en:
AFS Interkultur Danmark sends Danish young people (14-18+) to more than 60 countries on summer (4-5 weeks), trimester, semester and full-year programmes with host families.

The AFS Interkultur exchange scholarship (or the AFS Alumni DK scholarship - you may hold only one) supports school-programme participants who need financial help, based on household economy, social situation and motivation. It can be up to the normal participant fee but cannot be used for English-speaking destinations. Deadline for summer 2027 departures: 1 February 2027. Greenlandic students can also use NunaFonden and Sullissivik grants listed on the same page.

about.en:
ISEP is a non-profit network of universities in more than 50 countries. In ISEP Exchange you swap places with a student from another member institution: you pay tuition and fees to your home university (and usually housing and meals there, depending on the programme) and study abroad for a semester or year. You can list up to 10 universities and ISEP places you based on exchange space and your academic needs.

ISEP Direct is a separate, fee-based route where you pick a destination and pay a set fee that includes tuition, insurance and usually housing. To use ISEP your home university must be a member (check the member directory). Exchange applications for Semester 1 or full-year programmes starting July-October 2027 are due before 1 March 2027; priority deadlines are earlier.

en: Pay home tuition, study abroad
Choose up to 10 universities in 50+ countries
Fall 2027 deadline 1 March 2027

eligibility.en: Students enrolled at an ISEP member institution (check the member directory); requirements set by the home ISEP coordinator.

en: Check that your university is an ISEP member
Meet your ISEP coordinator
Choose up to 10 Exchange sites on search.isepstudyabroad.org
Submit the ISEP application before 1 March 2027 (or the priority deadline)
Receive placement and apply for visa

costs.en: Exchange: home-institution tuition and fees; ISEP application fee and personal costs. Direct: fixed programme fee.

score_reason: Affordable semester exchange, but only via member universities.

about.en:

about.en:
AFS Chile sends Chilean secondary students on school exchanges to about 40 countries (Africa, North America, Brazil, Asia, Europe and Oceania). Through its Solidarity Fund it supports more than 50% of school-exchange participants every year.

The Beca Ciudadano Global for 2027 school programmes covers about 90%, 70%, 50% or 30% of the programme price depending on family gross monthly income (up to CLP 1.5 million for 90%, up to 4.5 million for 30%) and grades (6.0+ for 30-50%, 6.5+ for 70-90% in 2023-2025). Selection includes a personal interview, a family interview, a group activity and a Sustainable Development Goals project. The scholarship application is separate from the programme application; contact AFS Chile for the closing date.

about.en:
Experiment e.V., Germany's oldest non-profit exchange organisation (95 years), awards a Jubilee Scholarship of up to 9,500 euros for a full school year abroad in any of its programme countries, departing summer 2027. Selection is based on financial situation and motivation: applicants submit a creative contribution (video, podcast, photo collage or similar) on how they would foster intercultural dialogue between the host country and Germany.

Apply online for an Experiment school year, then email the scholarship application and motivation letter to kortenbusch@experiment-ev.de by 30 November. Experiment also offers partial scholarships (up to 3,000 euros), Europe, climate and social-media scholarships with a 31 January deadline.

Partner funds include the Kreuzberger Kinderstiftung (up to 80% for non-Gymnasium students, mainly eastern Germany and Berlin, Europe only) and RuhrTalente. If you do not receive a scholarship you may withdraw free of charge within a set period.

about.en:
AFS Paraguay's open scholarships fund a full school year abroad for Paraguayan students with limited means: the Beca Completa Abierta covers 100% of the annual school programme and the Media Beca Abierta 50% (destination by availability; flights, visa, documents, school supplies and pocket money not covered). Recipients commit to volunteer with AFS in Paraguay for two years after returning.

In the 2026-27 cycle the call launched on 22 December 2025, opened on 5 January and closed on 30 January 2026, with an in-person evaluation day, family interviews and results on 23 February. Requirements were: 9th grade or 1st/2nd year of Media, average grade 5 in the last three years, financial need, leadership or community service, and a birth date window. The 2027-28 call is expected on the same schedule (launch late December 2026, deadline late January 2027).

Ilia State University (Tbilisi) has Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreements with universities across Europe. For the fall semester of 2026/27, applicants submitted a Learning Agreement to the faculty expert by 4 February 2026 and the application by 16 February 2026. A similar call for fall 2027 is expected in January-February 2027; specific partner calls (e.g. consortium places) can appear at other times. Check the IRO pages and contact erasmusplus@iliauni.edu.ge.

about.en:
Georgian Technical University (GTU) has Erasmus+ agreements with many European universities and announces each mobility as a separate competition on its 'Current Contests' page, stating the field, level, number of places and deadlines. Recent student calls included Mining/Geology/Petroleum at the University of Zagreb (2 places, 5 months), Business at Wittenborg UAS (7 places, with a 2-week internship), Business/IS/Finance/Architecture at the University of Liechtenstein, Architecture at ENSA Normandie (4 places), Food Science at Junia ISA Lille (2 master's places), Business/Economics at UMCS Lublin and Sapienza Rome.

Selection involves document submission, a foreign-language test and an interview with the competition committee; nominated students then register with the host university. Most mobilities carry an Erasmus+ grant (some are zero-grant). Fall-semester calls closed in March-April in 2026, so expect fall 2027 calls in spring 2027; GTU also runs weekly Erasmus+ consultations.

about.en:
The Fulbright UK Summer Institutes are the US-UK Fulbright Commission's flagship programme for American undergraduates. Each institute is a 3-4 week academic and cultural programme at a UK university; the 2026 institutes were Film at Lancaster University, 'Understanding Northern Ireland' at Queen's University Belfast and Scotland's History at the University of St Andrews (with Bristol and King's College London as partners).

The award covers round-trip airfare, airport transfer, tuition and fees, accommodation and some meals, the social and cultural programme and a small meal allowance; participants buy their own insurance. Eligibility (2026): U.S. citizens with a U.S. passport, little or no travel outside North America, GPA 3.6+, aged 18+ at the start and with at least two years of undergraduate study remaining. The 2026 cycle ran 11 November 2025 - 2 February 2026; the 2027 cycle is expected to follow the same pattern.

Applications expected mid-Nov 2026 to early Feb 2027

eligibility.en: U.S. citizens with a U.S. passport, GPA 3.6+, 18+ at start, at least two years of undergraduate study remaining, little or no experience outside North America; no other study abroad the same summer.

about.en:
IAESTE is a worldwide student-exchange association, founded in 1948, that swaps paid, career-focused internships between national committees. Employers in member countries offer placements, and each national committee nominates its own students for offers abroad. All internships are paid (examples on the platform: 2,350 EUR/month in Austria, 2,300 CHF/month in Switzerland, 15,000 KES/month in Kenya), and committees help with housing and visas.

Students register on the IAESTE Exchange Platform and contact their national or local committee, which sets eligibility and the selection timeline. Once selected and nominated, documents go to the employer for acceptance. Current listings show application deadlines between 6 November 2026 and 28 March 2027.

about.en:
Rotary Youth Exchange is Rotary International's long-term school exchange: a sponsoring Rotary club sends a student abroad for a school year, and a Rotary club in the host country arranges host families, school enrolment and a limited monthly spending allowance. Parents typically pay travel, health insurance and some other costs, while Rotary arranges travel and helps with visas; scholarships may be available in some cases.

In District 7390 the online application opened on 1 August 2026 and closes on 31 October 2026. Candidates then interview with their sponsoring club, attend district interviews on 14-15 November 2026 (with a mandatory day on 15 November to choose countries) and learn their host country on 31 January 2027. Students outside this district should contact their own local Rotary club, as every district runs its own timeline (usually autumn deadlines for the following year).
